correctness.rationale: Canonical primitive-line forms are unique; unit-root constraints and discriminant valuation classes are disjoint and exhaustive. Hensel root counts cover all k including the tangent case k=1 and k=2. The derived N0 makes the complete census. The maximum follows by comparing all positive sizes; the limit by a convergent geometric series. A fresh verifier exhaustively checks 292402 actual distinct lines across 15 cases and the first incidence moment. Unbounded proof is separate from finite tests.

originality.rationale: The distinctive assertion is an exact count of all primitive ring-affine lines by intersection multiplicity, not the previously known discriminant root counts or Euclidean collinearity upper bounds. The closest complete primary text (Khan et al., arXiv:1304.6943, §§1, especially Proposition 7) does prove the root-count ingredient and addresses Euclidean-line geometry, but does not state or imply the complete primitive ring-affine line census without new coefficient normalization, invertible-root exclusions, and discriminant-stratum enumeration. No covering result located in targeted searches; historical priority remains unverified.

value.rationale: The all-level primitive-line intersection distribution is a natural conic incidence invariant over finite chain rings, distinguishing tangent strata and governing exact sharp maximal intersection and line-type probabilities. Known quadratic root counts alone do not enumerate lines as subsets or give the whole incidence spectrum; the result includes ring normalization, root-unit exclusions and stable type densities. The finite-field arc case and its ring-prime-power breakdown have intrinsic geometric interest without an assumed downstream theorem.
